purpose: Add directly named freshwater source features from the Guinayangan Water District's 2024 report and check whether available aquaculture research supplies fish evidence for the separate De Guzman Fishpond lead.

sources.citation: Guinayangan Water District. Annual Report for Calendar Year 2024, including Annex J, List of Water Sources.
sources.access: Official 42-page PDF opened and reviewed through its report text; no local copy or geometry was retained.

sources.citation: Philippine Statistics Authority. Municipality of Guinayangan, PSGC barangay listing (as of 31 July 2025).
sources.access: Official PSA page opened; used only to check that source-named barangays belong to Guinayangan and to record their PSGC names/codes.

sources.citation: Saturno, A. (2024-01-29). FAC & CF Implement IDRC-funded Small-scale Aquaculture Action Research in Quezon Province. Central Luzon State University.
sources.access: Official university article opened and reviewed; no item-specific data reuse license was relied on.

method: Crosswalked Annex J's named water-source rows to the PSA barangay list without assigning coordinates or merging source names. Separately checked the exact De Guzman Fishpond name and reviewed the CLSU article as a possible municipal research lead; only a site is considered a match if the source identifies it explicitly.

sourceNamedWaterSources.name: Hinabaan River
sourceNamedWaterSources.decision: Added as a source-named river lead. The report lists it under surface-water sources; 'Flowing' is the water district's supply-status label, not an ecological flow, safety, or water-quality assessment.

deGuzmanFishpondScreen.exactNameSearch: Bounded public web searches for the exact pond name with Guinayangan/Quezon and fish/species terms did not surface an independently retrievable fish survey or species list explicitly tied to this pond. This is not evidence of fish absence.
deGuzmanFishpondScreen.clsuContext: The CLSU article reports a January 2024 municipality-level reconnaissance, visits to local aquaculture farms and seven unnamed lagoons, tilapia fingerling dispersal to smallholders, and a potential Fish Conservation Zone in Maulawin Spring Protected Landscape. It names no De Guzman Fishpond site, fish taxa, sampling stations, or fish survey results; no claim was assigned to the pond.

limitations: The report's Flowing/Yielding labels are operational water-supply statuses, not ecological flow measurements, potability findings, or safety advice.
The PSA source confirms administrative barangay names/codes only; neither it nor the water-district report supplies waterbody geometry or precise coordinates.
The Maulawin Spring Protected Landscape is not crosswalked to either named Maulawin spring source.
No fish occurrence, diet, catchability, access, or legal-fishing claim follows from water-supply or small-scale aquaculture context.
This source list is a municipality-level water-supply inventory, not a complete spring, river, lake, or fish inventory for Quezon or CALABARZON.
nextAction: Seek station-resolved, reusable fish surveys for the new river and spring leads; inspect any public Maulawin biodiversity monitoring outputs for fish-specific records; keep the De Guzman pond separate until an exact site/fish source is found.
